title: Oil Settles Near $86.5 Amid US-Iran Tensions
body: Crude oil pared earlier gains to settle near $86.50 a barrel on Wednesday, after briefly touching $88, rebounding from a 10-week low amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has reportedly relocated from his Washington residence to a military base for security reasons as Iranian threats intensify. According to reports, US officials have recently observed Iranian plots against American targets advancing to a more developed stage, and Bessent's prominent role in the US–Iran conflict has allegedly made him a primary target. Iranian officials have denied that any negotiations are taking place. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said assertions that talks are ongoing are intended to "ease economic pressures and reduce oil prices." Separately, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly stated that military action against Iran might not be required if existing economic sanctions and Washington's naval blockade remain effective. At the same time, Ukrainian drone attacks have disrupted Russian refineries accounting for roughly 30% of the country's total oil-processing capacity since late October, adding another layer of risk to global supply. title: Ibovespa Closes Higher on Fiscal Adjusment Prospects
body: The Ibovespa rose 0.4% on Wednesday, closing at 172,060 points, after markets reacted moderately positively to the first indications of the fiscal package President Lula is preparing for 2027. Planning Minister Simone Moretti stated that the bill's fiscal measures should generate an impact of R$50 billion to R$60 billion in 2027, with this effect increasing in subsequent years, and will give the government more tools to improve the primary balance. She also noted that the proposal would allow for additional spending freezes if necessary and affirmed that the government will "certainly" deliver a primary surplus in 2027. Among major banks, performance was mixed: Itaú rose 1.3%, while Banco do Brasil fell 1.2% ahead of its earnings release. Other financial stocks advanced, including B3, up 2.2%, and Itaúsa, up 1.5%. Utilities also gained, with Axia adding 0.6%. Petrobras declined 3.1% after its Q3 results, as net income came in below market expectations. In contrast, Vivo jumped 5.4% as it entered the fourth quarter with stronger sales momentum, and Rede D'Or rose 2.7% ahead of its earnings release scheduled for tomorrow. title: New Zealand Visitor Arrivals Growth Cools to 2.6% in Latest Monthly Read
body: New Zealand's visitor arrivals growth eased in the latest data release, with the month-over-month indicator slowing to 2.6% from a previously reported 3.0%. The figures, updated on 11 November 2026, show that while inbound tourism is still expanding, the pace of growth has moderated compared with the prior month. The data are measured on a month-over-month basis, meaning the current 2.6% figure reflects the change in visitor arrivals for the latest reported month relative to the previous one, while the 3.0% reading captured the change in the earlier month compared with its predecessor. The deceleration suggests a slightly softer, but still positive, trajectory for New Zealand's tourism momentum heading into the new period. title: New Zealand Long-Term Migration Rebounds in September, Edges Higher to 2,290 Arrivals
body: Permanent and long-term migration to New Zealand showed a modest uptick in September 2026, with net arrivals rising to 2,290, up from 2,260 in August 2026. The latest figures, updated on 11 November 2026, signal a continuation of gradual growth in inflows after the previous month's plateau. The 30-person increase between August and September, while relatively small in absolute terms, suggests that net long-term migration remains in positive territory and is inching higher rather than cooling off. This incremental gain may draw attention from businesses and policymakers tracking labour supply, housing demand and broader economic capacity as New Zealand heads toward the end of 2026. With the September 2026 reading now confirmed, markets and analysts will be watching upcoming releases for signs of whether this gentle upward trend solidifies into a stronger migration cycle or settles into a stable, moderate inflow. title: New Zealand Electronic Card Retail Growth Slows Sharply in October
body: New Zealand's electronic card retail sales growth eased notably in October 2026, signaling a loss of momentum in consumer spending. The latest figures, updated on 11 November 2026, show that while spending continues to expand compared with a year earlier, the pace of growth has weakened. The data are based on a year-over-year comparison, measuring October's performance against October a year ago, and September's against the same month a year earlier, highlighting a clear deceleration in electronic card-driven retail activity as the final quarter of 2026 begins. title: EU Stocks Rise to Record
body: European equities extended their winning streak on Wednesday, closing sharply higher for a third consecutive session on the back of robust technology earnings. The Euro STOXX 50 advanced 1% to 6,393, while the STOXX Europe 600 climbed 0.7% to a record high of 663.1. The technology sector led gains as it continued to rebound from last week's selloff. Sentiment improved following stronger-than-expected results from US-based CoreWeave, which helped ease concerns that the elevated debt levels among AI companies could constrain further investment in the sector. Siemens Energy also contributed to the upbeat mood, rising after surging data center demand boosted its margins in the latest quarter, lifting both profits and guidance. AI infrastructure suppliers benefited from the improved outlook, with ASML gaining 3.2% and Infineon jumping 6.4%. Financials were another source of support. Banks extended their advance, with Deutsche Bank up 2% and ING adding 1.3%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Brazil Swings to FX Outflows as Foreign Exchange Flows Reverse by Over $11 Billion
body: Brazil's foreign exchange flows have sharply reversed, shifting from a robust surplus to a notable deficit, according to the latest data updated on 11 November 2026. The indicator, which previously stood at a positive $9.498 billion, has now fallen to a negative $2.059 billion. This turnaround represents a swing of more than $11 billion and signals that, on net, foreign currency is leaving Brazil rather than entering. While the data alone does not specify the underlying drivers, such a move typically raises investor attention given its potential implications for liquidity in the FX market, corporate funding conditions, and the trajectory of the Brazilian real. Market participants will be watching subsequent releases closely to assess whether this marks the beginning of a sustained trend of outflows or a temporary adjustment in cross-border capital movements and trade-related FX operations. title: Swiss Franc futures tumble to worst day since March.
body: Swiss Franc futures declined sharply against the U.S. dollar, dropping 1.06% to an intraday low of 1.2040 to register their largest single-day percentage decline since March 2. Greenback strength expanded after core CPI increased 0.3% month over month, hitting the threshold Fed Governor Christopher Waller indicated would open discussion for a 50 bps move. The CME FedWatch Tool now fully prices a December policy increase, reflecting an 86.9% probability of a 25 bps hike and a 13.1% chance of a half-point adjustment. Meanwhile, the Swiss National Bank maintains its policy rate at zero with inflation remaining contained, setting up potential further policy divergence between the two central banks.

title: 10-Year T-Note futures slip as rate hike expectations firm.
body: December 10-Year T-Note futures traded down to 106'000 during a holiday-shortened session, pointing to higher implied yields as markets continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and hawkish rhetoric from Federal Reserve officials. Pricing across interest rate futures reflected growing expectations for policy tightening at the December FOMC meeting, with market-derived probabilities solidifying around a 25 bps hike alongside emerging odds for a 50 bps move. Meanwhile, CVOL held largely unchanged with the cash Treasury market shuttered for Veterans Day. Market attention now turns to Thursday's 30-Year Treasury bond auction, initial jobless claims data, existing home sales figures and multiple scheduled appearances by Fed policymakers.

title: Live Cattle Futures Ease as Screwworm Facility Progresses
body: Live Cattle futures declined across the board as advancing progress on the new screwworm facility bolstered market confidence ahead of its scheduled April 2027 opening. A sharp jump in corn prices applied further downward pressure across the beef complex. The December Live Cattle contract fell $1.83 to settle at $217.37, while February bounced from session lows of $221.02. In Feeder Cattle futures, trading ended mixed as forecasts for reduced beef production contended with softer cash pricing. The January contract advanced $3.45 to $330.12, marking an $18 gain from Friday lows. Lean Hog futures held steady in sideways consolidation following the latest WASDE release. Stronger domestic pork demand projections helped counter weak export cutouts, lifting the December contract to a $56 close.

title: E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures test 200-day average on tech rally.
body: E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures surged to test the 200-day moving average after four consecutive closes below that benchmark level. December futures climbed to an intraday peak of 28,697 before consolidating near 28,532, supported by strong third-quarter earnings and an upgraded full-year outlook from CoreWeave that eased market concerns regarding artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Meanwhile, with the cash Treasury market closed for Veterans Day, December 10-Year T-Note futures slipped 0.2%, pointing to higher implied yields as Fed funds futures fully priced expectations for a December policy hike.

title: Soybean and wheat futures advance as corn retreats.
body: Soybean futures extended their post-WASDE advance, rising eight cents to settle at 1236'0 and bringing two-day gains to 51 cents as the USDA raised export forecasts and trimmed ending stocks. Option open interest expanded across calls and puts, while CVOL stood at 14.6%. Corn futures retreated as weaker demand forecasts for feed and exports offset lower carryout figures, with December corn futures dropping 5 3/4 cents before closing at 447'2 amid heavy call open interest. Wheat futures found technical support from oversold levels, lifting December Chicago wheat above 600'0 to reach 603'6 while Kansas City December wheat climbed to 643'6.
